parole.significato: A member of a class of rich high-caste (Brahmin) landlords in Bengal formed during the British Raj.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Bengali ভদ্রলোক (bhodrolōk, “gentleman”), from Sanskrit भद्र (bhadra) + लोक (loka).

parole.significato: A small open boat, propelled by oars or paddles, carried as a tender, lifeboat, or pleasure craft on a ship.
parole.testo: From Bengali ডিঙি (ḍiṅi), perhaps from Sanskrit द्रोण (droṇa, “wooden trough”).

parole.significato: Bos frontalis, a Southern Asiatic species of domestic cattle.
parole.testo: From Bengali গয়াল (goẏal), from Sanskrit गौ॒रः (gauráḥ) or Sanskrit गौः (gauḥ). Doublet of gaur.

parole.significato: A body comprising all the voters of gram panchayat constituency, meeting at the behest of the head of the panchayat to…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Bengali গ্রাম সংসদ (gram śoṅśod, literally “village parliament”), which is a learned borrowing from Sanskrit ग्राम (grāma) + संसद (saṃsada).

parole.significato: An ethnic group belonging to the Bodo-Kachari group of peoples; one of the scheduled tribes of India.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Bengali মেচ (mec), from Sanskrit म्ले॒च्छ (mlecchá). Doublet of mleccha.

parole.significato: A spicy grilled South Indian curry made with chillis and ginger.
parole.testo: Likely from Bengali ফাল (phal), metathesis of লাফ (laph), from Sanskrit लम्फ (lampha).
